title: Tales of the Alhambra
author: Washington Irving
description: In 1829 the American writer Washington Irving lived for a few months in empty rooms of the Alhambra, then half ruined. His sketches and Moorish legends made it famous, and his rooms overlooked this garden courtyard.

title: The Alhambra
author: Robert Irwin
description: A short, sharp guide to the Alhambra by the historian Robert Irwin: who built it, how it was used, and how much of what visitors see was invented by later restorers and romantic writers.

title: Granada
author: Radwa Ashour
description: The Egyptian novelist Radwa Ashour follows a family of bookbinders in the Albaicín after the Christian conquest of 1492, as their language, religion, and books are taken from them. Translated into English in 2003.

title: Blood and Faith
author: Matthew Carr
description: Matthew Carr’s history of the Moriscos, the Muslims forced to become Christian after 1492, from the broken promises of Granada’s surrender to their mass expulsion from Spain between 1609 and 1614.

title: The Moor’s Last Sigh
author: Salman Rushdie
description: Salman Rushdie’s novel about a family in Bombay. Its title comes from Boabdil, Granada’s last sultan, who is said to have looked back and sighed at this mountain pass on his way into exile in 1492.

title: Gypsy Ballads
author: Federico García Lorca
description: The book of poems that made Lorca famous: ballads of Andalusian Romani life, the Civil Guard, the moon, and death, written in the language of folk song. Lorca later tired of being known as the Gypsy poet.

title: The Assassination of Federico García Lorca
author: Ian Gibson
description: The Irish historian Ian Gibson’s investigation into Lorca’s arrest and killing in August 1936. An earlier version came out in Paris in 1971, because it was banned in Franco’s Spain. Gibson later wrote Lorca’s biography.

title: South from Granada
author: Gerald Brenan
description: The English writer Gerald Brenan’s memoir of the 1920s in Yegen, a village in the Alpujarra, the mountain valleys south of Granada. Friends from the Bloomsbury group, including Virginia Woolf, came to visit.
